extracted.intended_audience: newsrooms, reporters, editors, producers, and students preparing submissions for the Online Journalism Awards (OJA)
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions of eligibility, judging criteria, format/length rules, and evidence requested for entries to the Online Journalism Awards across all categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News — judged dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will weigh evidence of exceptional journalism, quality of writing and creative use of digital, social and mobile platforms under deadline pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All work submitted must have been produced within 72 hours of the original news event. Entrants are strongly encouraged to provide screenshots or other evidence from the first minutes and hours after the event to clarify publication times and how coverage developed over time. Two awards: Small/Medium newsroom; Large newsroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News — production timeframe requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All work submitted must have been produced within 72 hours of the original news event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence (screenshots or other) from the first minutes and hours after the event to clarify publication times and how coverage developed over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Video Storytelling — distinction of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will consider the distinction of presentation, how the work incorporates digital storytelling techniques and is unique to digital platforms and the impact of the journalism produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention will also be paid to innovative use of digital video, and creativity used to tell stories on digital, mobile and social platforms. In all subcategories, credits do not count towards total overall length of the video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Video Storytelling — format/time categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries judged by subcategory: Social Media (videos <3 minutes), Short Form (≤10 minutes), Long Form (>10 minutes), Series (three videos any length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social Media may submit up to 3 videos as a package. Series: three videos of any length within a series; no time limit on videos in the series. Each subcategory has Small/Medium and Large newsroom awards (and Social Media separate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in AI Innovation — purpose & evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will be evaluated on the extent to which their AI implementation serves an identified need, either internally or externally focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges also weigh quality of the entry on creative use of AI tools, considerations for human agency in the design and how the tools improve the human experience. Entrants are strongly encouraged to submit up to five URLs and an in-depth explanation on how they used generative-AI tools to enhance their work. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Audio Digital Storytelling — journalistic & production criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will consider the journalism behind an audio project, the uniqueness and originality of voice, overall production quality, and innovative use of storytelling techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention to creativity in telling stories that are truly of digital and mobile platforms. Four awards by format: ongoing series, limited series, daily/weekly news, use of audio storytelling. Entries may include up to three URLs linking to the audio media as specified per subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Collaboration and Partnerships — required documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should include documentation from each partner in the collaboration and partnership, covering the contributions from various entities that made the collaboration a success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A winning entry should show creativity and innovation through a partnership that resulted in outstanding journalism and unique storytelling approaches using digital media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Newsletters — voice and format criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should showcase a unique voice, whether the newsletter is issued by an individual or organization, and may span a wide array of newsletter formats (digest, curated resources, ideas/opinions, original reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should note visual elements that regularly accompany stories. Entries may consist of daily, weekly or other regularly delivered offerings; reasonable gaps are allowed. Judges will consider quality of writing, design, frequency, length of content based on the material, subject matter and overall strategy and impact of the newsletter. Two awards: Single Newsletter and Portfolio (up to five URLs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Science Reporting — judging dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will weigh the overall quality and integrity of the journalism and editorial process, the use of facts in an easily understandable way for the identified audiences, digital production and design of the coverage, and the ways in which the engagement and delivery strategy was employed to reach, inform and engage with the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may report across health, climate, space, STEM, etc., and may include writing, photography, data visualization, video or audio. Entries may include up to three links demonstrating how a single story used multiple mediums to reach intended audiences. Two awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Social Justice Reporting — topic scope and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: This award honors works that highlight systemic inequities encountered by marginalized/underrepresented communities; examples include social movements, racial justice, voting rights, migration, LGBTQ+ issues, gender equity, access to education, food or healthcare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will weigh the quality of the journalism, digital innovation, engagement strategy and the impact of the project. Two awards: Single Story and Portfolio (portfolios may include up to 5 links).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Social Media Engagement — evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will evaluate entries on journalistic excellence, execution of the identified engagement strategy, and overall impact of the story or project on the intended community or audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may include reporting repackaged for social media or original social-media-first content and assets from any medium. Entrants may submit up to five links. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Sports Reporting — standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful entries will demonstrate the highest journalistic standards, digital production and coverage design, and the ways in which digital, social, mobile and other platforms are employed to reach, inform and engage the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may cover professional/amateur sports, athlete profiles, trends, investigations. Two awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Technology Reporting — evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will weigh the quality of the journalism, digital production and design, use of platforms, engagement strategy and the impact of the coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may address technology culture, policy, economic impact, and include investigations, analysis, or profiles across formats. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Visual Digital Storytelling — visual criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will consider the quality and impact of the visuals, the selection of media and the effectiveness of the visuals in conveying the story’s topic or event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention to originality, innovation and creativity in storytelling truly of digital and mobile platforms; may include VR, AI, chatbots, AR, MR, 360 video, emerging media. Visual storytelling often has reporting/text as a component. Awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory Reporting — sustained coverage criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should cover a planned, significant news event or topic over a sustained period of time, and explain the relevance and impact of a subject or event to audiences through storytelling and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges consider execution and quality of the journalism; design and presentation; and ways in which multiple platforms, including social and mobile, were used to reach, inform and engage the audience. Entries should consist of up to five work samples. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature — depth and engagement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors a single package or story that shows significant depth, insight and new understanding of a story or topic; may be profiles, feature packages, or watchdog journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will consider use of social tools to build participatory online community, quality of journalism, digital production and design, and use of multiple platforms to reach, inform and engage. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather Award in Community-Centered Journalism — core emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should emphasize: how the approach understood how journalism could best serve identified communities; which communities were targeted and why; how decisions were made to engage communities; and how the project established meaningful pathways for community contribution to reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include links to stories and supporting materials demonstrating impact, post-project reflections (up to 500 words), and/or documented conversations with community members. Judges consider intentional design of engagement strategies, innovative uses of engagement platforms, adaptability of approaches and meaningful impact. Entries must explicitly state what makes the work unusually effective in serving a specific community. Two project awards based on communities served (Urban & National Focus; Community-Based & Rural Focus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather Award — urban vs rural definitions & judging context
rubrics_metrics.description: Urban communities include metropolitan areas with populations of 50,000+ and broader audiences served by national or multi-city efforts; rural communities include less densely populated areas and smaller or tightly connected communities within urban settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental criteria remain the same for both categories, but judges take into account distinct contexts: urban/national judges consider complex, diverse information needs; rural/community judges consider resource limitations, geographic isolation, and unique dynamics. Newsrooms should apply based on primary audience served, not physical location.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Excellence in Online Journalism — judged dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries will be judged on quality of journalism, a superb user experience and the use of social tools and other digital media to reach, inform and engage audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category honors a digitally focused news organization that successfully fulfills its editorial mission, serves its audience, maximizes digital tools, and represents highest journalistic standards. Four awards by newsroom size (including micro).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in Revenue Strategy — evaluation focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will be evaluated on the extent to which their revenue innovation serves an identified need and contributes to the operation’s sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may include subscription models, membership programs, events, branded content, merchandising, licensing, partnerships. Entrants are strongly encouraged to submit up to five URLs and an in-depth explanation on development and implementation. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knight Award for Public Service — public service impact & community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries will be judged on techniques and resources deployed to engage the community in the reporting process and the use of digital media storytelling to compile, analyze and/or present critical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special emphasis on journalism that builds trust within the identified community or addresses critical issues in underserved communities in innovative ways; judges look for storytelling that makes an impact and motivates audience to act. Entries may be a single package or continuing project, may include one main URL and up to four supporting URLs. Evidence of public service impact should be provided in the entry description. One award ($5,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Commentary — voice, writing and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will consider the quality of the writing and presentation, social strategies to attract user response or action and overall impact of the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honors a unique and powerful voice original to the web; entries may include text, audio, videos, graphics, podcasts. Print-first content after initial digital posting is allowed but print-first content that was first published in print is not eligible. Two awards: Personal Narrative (first-person single story) and Package of Columns (up to five URLs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Commentary — personal narrative criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Narrative honors a single first-person story where the writer’s life experience or intimate view is the main focus; judges consider creativity of storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry type limited to single story; judged for voice and creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Journalism Award — eligibility & criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors work produced by high school or undergraduate students that uses digital storytelling and technologies; judges consider quality of journalism, digital production and design, and use of platforms to reach and engage audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may submit 2–5 links highlighting projects. Entrants must submit a short (1 page max) letter of recommendation from a professor or professional in support of the student and the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Al Neuharth Innovation in Investigative Journalism — evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges consider clear presentation through user interface and interactivity, creative use of the medium and platforms (including mobile), use of social tools and evidence of the impact of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges also consider impact through subsequent coverage, conversations or resulting policy changes. An entry consists of a single piece, series or package on the same subject, including an explanation detailing the investigation’s impact. Up to five examples may be submitted. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Florida Award for Investigative Data Journalism — data-focused criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This award will focus on the effectiveness of the data to tell a story, how well the data is presented to users, the journalistic impact and relevance of the data, and the design and functionality of the data presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will also take into account the difficulty in acquiring the data. Winners attend workshops. Two awards by newsroom size with $7,500 prize each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical Reporting: Artificial Intelligence — core goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes clarity, accuracy, and transparency in reporting on AI, elevating journalism that educates and informs the public through clear communication that eschews tired tropes and promotes nuanced public discourse about AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may be articles, videos, podcasts, interactives or visual communications but all must have a target reading or engagement time of less than 20 minutes (section under consideration must be <20 minutes; denote timecodes for audio/video). Provide a short statement explaining how submission fulfills the goals and criteria. Four awards by newsroom size; early-bird fee waiver noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical Reporting: AI — specific judging emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will consider: clear and accessible descriptions of AI (human actors, jargon-free language, context-appropriate imagery); grounded discussion of AI capabilities (specific about type of AI, design context, limitations); and journalistic transparency & representativeness (well-rounded sourcing, fact-checking, appropriate context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to past winners of Aspen Digital’s “Reporting on Hall of Fame” for examples of approach; entrants encouraged to provide statement and timecodes as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical Reporting: Gender and Identity — evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will weigh the quality of the journalism, digital production and design, use of platforms, engagement strategy and the impact of the coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may address politics, workplace, health, safety, lifestyle, economic impact, reproductive rights, sports, education, media representation and culture; formats include investigations, analysis and profiles across media. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical Reporting: Immigration — evaluation criteria and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will weigh the quality of the journalism, digital production and design, use of platforms, engagement strategy and the impact of the coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may address policy and enforcement, asylum and legal systems, labor and economy, health, education, community impact, border security, diaspora communities, human stories; local, national or international perspectives allowed. Three awards by newsroom size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-submission honoree awards — selection basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain awards (Impact Award, James Foley Award for Conflict Reporting, ONA Community Award, Rich Jaroslovsky Founder Award) are not open for submission; honorees are recommended and selected by committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions explain the kinds of contributions or impact the committee will look for (e.g., lasting contributions to digital journalism, tools/environments supporting journalists, trailblazing individual impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry-specific URLs and supporting materials guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Many categories strongly encourage or permit entrants to submit up to a specified number of URLs (commonly up to five; some categories up to three or four) and supporting materials such as screenshots, archives, links, or timecodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each category's stated limits (e.g., AI Innovation: up to five URLs and in-depth explanation; Audio: up to three URLs; newsletters: up to five URLs; Topical AI: denote timecodes and ensure target section <20 minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and length constraints across categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Several categories set format/time constraints (e.g., Digital Video Storytelling social media videos <3 minutes; Short Form ≤10 minutes; Long Form >10 minutes; Topical AI target engagement <20 minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submitted section fits the category's length rules and clearly denote timecodes for audio/video submissions as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of digital platforms and multi-platform engagement as a cross-cutting criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Across many categories judges consider how multiple platforms (digital, mobile, social) were used to reach, inform and engage the audience; use of social tools and engagement strategies is repeatedly weighed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe engagement strategy, platforms used, and evidence of audience impact where possible (metrics, community feedback, examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of journalism and editorial standards as universal criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Most categories require judges to evaluate the quality of the journalism: reporting rigor, accuracy, integrity, sourcing, clarity and storytelling craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation of editorial process, fact-checking, sourcing, and examples that demonstrate journalistic standards and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation, originality and creativity as a recurring criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Many categories reward innovation in storytelling, presentation, use of technology (including AI), revenue strategies, partnerships, or engagement techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the work is innovative or original, cite new techniques or approaches, and provide examples or metrics showing effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — evidence of outcomes or change
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges often weigh evidence of impact (public service impact, policy changes, subsequent coverage, audience action, community outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence of impact in the entry description: follow-up coverage, policy change documentation, audience feedback, or other measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design, UX and presentation as evaluative factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges consider digital production and design, user interface and interactivity, and the effectiveness of presentation in conveying the story or data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For data and visual categories, emphasize design, functionality, and clarity for users; include examples or links demonstrating UI/interactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing, representativeness and transparency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories (notably Topical AI and others) emphasize well-rounded sourcing, fact-checking, and transparency to earn audience trust and provide appropriate context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain sourcing strategy, fact-checking processes, and how representativeness was achieved; provide supporting documentation if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility & rules pointer
rubrics_metrics.description: Please read entry requirements carefully. Entries in some categories require more information. For detailed eligibility requirements, see the Rules & Eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced Rules & Eligibility page for category-specific eligibility, deadlines, and other procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging by newsroom size segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many awards are split by newsroom size (micro, small, medium, large) with separate awards for each tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check category listing for which size tiers apply and apply in the tier appropriate to your newsroom (e.g., General Excellence has Small, Medium, Large, Micro).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of community engagement and constituent contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: For community-centered and public service awards, entries should document how communities were engaged and how community members contributed to reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable materials include post-project reflections, transcripts, audio/video snippets, or written summaries; concise statements suffice if capacity for materials is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data difficulty and provenance for data journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges consider the difficulty in acquiring data and the provenance/credibility of data sources for investigative and data journalism awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document data sources, acquisition challenges, cleaning/analysis methods, and provide links or examples of data presentation and interactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package and portfolio submission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Some categories accept packages or portfolios rather than a single piece and specify limits (e.g., Digital Video Storytelling Series = three videos; Commentary package = up to five URLs; Student entries 2–5 links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow per-category limits and label components clearly in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special funds and fee waivers guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some categories or applicant groups have financial support or fee waivers (e.g., Podcasting, Seriously Awards Fund supports independent audio producers; Aspen Digital waives submission fees for Topical Reporting: AI during early bird).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying applicants should follow fund application instructions; refer to category text for reimbursement or waiver details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant documentation of methods & process
rubrics_metrics.description: Several categories request or encourage an in-depth explanation of methods, workflows, or implementation (e.g., AI Innovation and Revenue Strategy encourage in-depth explanations of how tools or strategies were developed and implemented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear narratives of development, implementation, human-in-the-loop considerations, metrics of success, and links to examples where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special attention to accessibility and serving underserved audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Some awards (Gather, Knight Award, AI Innovation where accessibility is mentioned) encourage attention to accessibility and serving traditionally underserved or unheard communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document accessibility features, translation/language strategies, platform choices made to meet audience needs, and evidence of effectiveness for those communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timecode and excerpt requirements for longer media
rubrics_metrics.description: When submissions contain long-form media, the category may require that the section under consideration be less than a specified engagement time and that timecodes be denoted for audio/video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical AI requires target reading/engagement time <20 minutes for the section under consideration and timecodes must be denoted for audio/video formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit and runtime accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: For video categories, credits do not count towards total overall length of the video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure runtime calculations exclude credits when considering category length limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' focus on newsroom strategy and sustainability (General & Revenue categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: General Excellence and Innovation in Revenue Strategy evaluate organizational strategy: how the newsroom fulfills mission, uses digital tools, and implements revenue innovations that sustain and expand journalistic work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide metrics, strategy descriptions, examples of audience growth or financial outcomes, and supporting URLs where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant responsibility to state what makes work unusually effective
rubrics_metrics.description: For community-centered or engagement-focused categories, entries need to explicitly state what makes the submitted work unusually effective in terms of better serving a specific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly articulate differentiators, outcomes, and evidence rather than assuming judges will infer them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations around print-first content for commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries consisting of online publication of print-first content are not eligible for Online Commentary; print syndication after initial digital posting does not disqualify an entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure commentary is original to the web or was first published digitally to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize and award amount disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Some categories disclose monetary prizes or special perks (e.g., General Excellence $5,000 per tier, University of Florida awards $7,500 per tier, Gather category $2,500 project prize).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize information is listed per category; consult the category text for exact amounts and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission support for independent creators
rubrics_metrics.description: The Podcasting, Seriously Awards Fund and similar sponsors support independent producers by covering submission fees or reimbursing applicants under qualifying conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent U.S., U.K., Canada, and Australia-based audio professionals can apply for reimbursement; the Fund disburses at least $20,000 annually and supports 200+ submissions a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact documentation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where impact is a criterion, entries should provide concrete evidence: follow-up reporting, policy outcomes, community testimonials, audience metrics, or other demonstrable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples suggested for Gather include newsroom reflections, short video of community members discussing impact, or written audience feedback; concise statements acceptable if capacity limited.
